function: Learned joint design of pilots, user-side channel-feature extraction with RVQ-VAE feedback, and EGAT multi-user precoding, scalable to feedback bits and user count (p. 1, 4).
system: Downlink FDD massive MIMO: BS with M=128 dual-polarized UPA antennas serves K=3-8 single-antenna users at 3.5 GHz; no RIS (p. 3, 10-12).
method: Pilot layer, FCN extractor, RVQ-VAE (NSVQ) feedback and EGAT graph-attention precoder, trained jointly on negative sum-rate plus quantization MSE (unsupervised); progressive stage-wise training with fine-tuning (p. 5-8).
data_channel: Own ray-tracing dataset from Remcom Wireless InSite: 128 areas of 128x128 m, 3.5 GHz, M=128; 100,000 training, 18,000 validation, 10,000 test channels (p. 10).
test_conditions: Trained once at B=30, tested at B_deploy 5-30 by codebook shrinkage; one network for K=3-8; train 20 dB, test other SNRs; 5 unseen ray-traced environments (p. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: ZF with perfect CSIT, ZF with LMMSE estimate and perfect feedback, ZF with Lloyd-RVQ feedback. Learned: DL method of [6]; E2E-trained variant (p. 10-11).
metrics: Sum-rate versus SNR, feedback bits, number of users, RVQ stages and unseen environments; quantization complexity log(N 2^(B/N)) and share of codewords used (p. 11-13).
complexity: Quantization complexity as number of codewords: N 2^(B/N) versus 2^B; B=15, N=3 uses 0.29% of codewords; no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime of the full network (p. 6, 12).
openness: Code: https://github.com/LINZHU-PolyU/Scalable-Precoding-MU-MIMO (p. 11, footnote 3); dataset generated with commercial Remcom Wireless InSite, no data link.
q1_support: p. 10: "we can use the ray-tracing simulator to generate the user channels". Own Remcom Wireless InSite scenes (128 areas); not DeepMIMO, 3GPP, COST 2100 or measured data, despite "real-world dataset" in the abstract (p. 1).
q2_support: p. 12: "for testing, we include 5 additional unseen environments, which are also modeled using ray-tracing". Also trained once at B=30 and tested at B_deploy 5-30 (p. 11).
q3_support: p. 11: "the proposed model significantly outperforms the DL-based method in [6], particularly in high SNR regimes". [6] is an earlier learned joint pilot, feedback and precoding design; the ZF baselines with LMMSE or Lloyd quantization (p. 10) are non-learned; all on sum-rate (Fig. 5).
q4_support: p. 12: "characterize the quantization complexity using log(N 2B/N )" and "while using only 0.29% of the codewords". Codeword count of the quantizer only; no FLOPs, parameters or runtime for the full network.
q5_support: p. 11: "Our code can be found in https://github.com/LINZHU-PolyU/Scalable-Precoding-MU-MIMO" (footnote 3). Channels come from commercial ray tracing; no data link.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2504.11162) titled 'Scalable Transceiver Design for Multi-User Communication in FDD Massive MIMO Systems via Deep Learning'; it prints no journal DOI, so the DOI-title match cannot be checked from the file. Area 3 chosen over 2 because the loss and every result metric is sum-rate (p. 8, 11-13) and the implicit feedback features are never scored by channel reconstruction error; area 2 is the alternative since the RVQ-VAE feedback is the main novelty, so the reviewer may confirm. q1 is 0 because the abstract and conclusion say 'real-world dataset', but Section VI-A (p. 10) shows synthetic Wireless InSite ray tracing of the authors' own scenes; confirm it is not a shared dataset. q4 rests on the quantizer codeword count only (p. 12), so the reviewer may confirm. Table I (p. 13) compares the proposed method only with the two ZF baselines in unseen environments.
